def hop_game(a, tokens):
    """Two players, Alice and Bob, play a game on a paper strip of n cells,
    numbered 0 to n-1 from left to right. Cell i has a printed number a[i].
    Tokens stand on the strip: tokens[j] is the cell of the j-th token, and
    several tokens may occupy the same cell.

    Alice moves first and the players alternate turns. A move consists of
    picking any single token, say on cell i, choosing a hop length d with
    1 <= d <= min(a[i], i), and sliding that token left to cell i - d.
    (A token on cell 0, or on a cell with a[i] == 0, can never be moved.)
    A player who has no legal move on their turn loses. Both players play
    optimally.

    If Bob wins, return the string 'LOSE'. If Alice wins, return one winning
    first move as a tuple (p, q) of ints, meaning 'move a token from cell p
    to cell q'. Among ALL winning first moves, return the one with the
    smallest p, and among those the one with the smallest q.

    Constraints: 1 <= n <= 200 where n = len(a); 0 <= a[i] <= n;
    1 <= len(tokens) <= 200; 0 <= tokens[j] <= n-1. The number of tokens may
    be large, so exploring the game tree over all token configurations is
    infeasible.

    >>> hop_game([0, 1], [1])
    (1, 0)
    >>> hop_game([0, 1], [1, 1])
    'LOSE'
    >>> hop_game([0, 1, 2, 1, 1, 3], [3, 4, 5])
    (3, 2)
    """
